goal: Implements OP_CAT (BIP-347) as a Tapscript opcode with activation flags, without enabling activation itself.
Lets developers test and build on top of OP_CAT ahead of any future activation decision, and adds reusable Tapscript test tooling.
reviewability: Paused: converted to draft by a maintainer explicitly because there is no rough consensus yet on the concept of OP_CAT itself.
Author has been silent 120+ days and recently said attention is shifting elsewhere, so reviewing code now risks being invalidated by a still-open concept decision.
agreement: Disputed at the concept level: achow101 moved the PR to draft citing lack of consensus after a CoreDev Kill/Shill/Merge session (achow101).

No reviewer has issued a blocking code objection, and code-level questions (ajtowns, awin28522, rot13maxi) were addressed, but the higher-level activation question remains unresolved and unanswered by the author recently.

result.summary: This PR implements OP_CAT as a new Tapscript opcode per BIP-347, redefining OP_SUCCESS126, along with the SCRIPT_VERIFY_OP_CAT and SCRIPT_VERIFY_DISCOURAGE_OP_CAT flags that a future soft fork could use to activate it. It explicitly does not include any activation or signaling logic. It adds a large JSON script-test suite for OP_CAT, unit tests, a functional test, and new macros (#SCRIPT#, #CONTROLBLOCK#) that make writing Tapscript JSON script tests much easier.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core currently has no reference implementation of OP_CAT for developers, researchers, or downstream forks (e.g. bitcoin-inquisition/signet) to build and test against, and no consensus code exists to evaluate whether a future CAT soft fork would be correct if activated.

open_concerns: Whether there is community/maintainer consensus for the concept of OP_CAT in Tapscript at all (achow101, moved to draft after a CoreDev Kill/Shill/Merge session).

moonsettler proposed a 'neutered CAT' with an 80-byte output cap as a compromise; bigspider argued this does not actually prevent the introspection tricks the cap is meant to block, since sub-32-byte hash pieces can already be built and CAT would just reassemble them.

ajtowns raised a clarification about the SCRIPT_VERIFY_OP_CAT/DISCOURAGE_OP_CAT truth table for pre/post activation relay and block validation, addressed by later discussion but not obviously merged into the PR text.
resolved_concerns: rot13maxi's request for tests covering combinations of SCRIPT_VERIFY_OP_CAT, SCRIPT_VERIFY_DISCOURAGE_OP_CAT and SCRIPT_VERIFY_DISCOURAGE_OP_SUCCESS was implemented by the author with additional JSON test cases.
Co1nB3e's question about the OP_CAT=false/DISCOURAGE_OP_CAT=false edge case was answered by EthanHeilman and arminsabouri (this is the pre-activation block-validation case and is already tested).
discussion.author_status: active intermittently via force-pushes through 2026-05-16, but silent on substantive discussion since 2026-05-09; EthanHeilman (co-contributor) said on 2026-04-30 he is shifting attention to quantum-computing concerns and will return in 2026

reviewability.label: Awaiting concept consensus
reviewability.reason: A maintainer (achow101) explicitly converted this to draft because there is no rough consensus yet on activating OP_CAT in Tapscript, following a CoreDev Kill/Shill/Merge session, and said the PR cannot be merged even if the code is fine until that changes. No one has since indicated consensus has formed, and the author/co-contributor have both signaled reduced attention, so a code review now risks being moot if the concept direction shifts.

agreement.summary: Concept-level dispute: achow101 says there's no consensus for OP_CAT yet and drafted the PR; code-level review comments were addressed by the author.
agreement.reason: The disagreement here is not about the code's correctness (reviewers who engaged, ajtowns, rot13maxi, awin28522, had their points addressed) but about whether the network/project wants a CAT soft fork at all, which a maintainer says is unresolved. That is exactly the kind of open activation question the validation category treats as P1-worthy to resolve, but it also means the PR is currently blocked on a decision rather than on code quality.
evidence: achow101: 'there does not appear to be consensus for the concept of OP_CAT in TapScript yet, so this PR cannot be merged even if the code is okay,' citing a CoreDev Kill/Shill/Merge session.
moonsettler proposed a size-limited 'neutered CAT' compromise; bigspider countered that this doesn't achieve the stated goal.
rot13maxi's and Co1nB3e's technical questions were answered and, where actionable, implemented by the author (additional test cases).

enables: Downstream soft-fork activation logic for OP_CAT, if the community reaches consensus (explicitly out of scope here).
Reusable #SCRIPT#/#CONTROLBLOCK# JSON test macros that make future Tapscript script_tests.json additions much easier to write.

categories.name: validation
categories.evidence: Adds a new Tapscript opcode implementation and two new script verify flags directly in src/script/interpreter.cpp/.h, changing what OP_SUCCESS126 evaluates to and adding a new consensus-adjacent error path; carries the Consensus label.
categories.rationale: Per the validation category rubric, proposed soft forks are P1-worthy because of the importance of reaching a decision and of the code being correct if ever activated, not because of a judgment on whether the fork should happen. A maintainer explicitly paused the PR pending exactly that consensus decision, which is the category-defining blocker described here.

categories.name: mempool
categories.evidence: Adds SCRIPT_VERIFY_DISCOURAGE_OP_CAT to STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS in src/policy/policy.h, which controls whether nodes relay/accept OP_CAT-using transactions pre-activation.
categories.rationale: The policy change is a no-op today (arminsabouri: 'By default, the SCRIPT_VERIFY_DISCOURAGE_OP_CAT bit is set, and we do not expose this as a configurable mempool policy'), so it has no immediate DoS or relay impact; its value is entirely contingent on a future activation decision that is itself unresolved.

categories.name: tests
categories.evidence: Adds ~414 lines of new JSON script tests, three new C++ unit tests (cat_simple, cat_empty_stack, cat_dup_test), a new functional test feature_opcat.py, and new #SCRIPT#/#CONTROLBLOCK# macros in script_tests.cpp that generalize how Tapscript JSON tests are written.
categories.rationale: The description states the macros solve a real gap: 'no one has added any Tapscript tests to JSON script tests until this PR' because computing control blocks and outputs by hand was prohibitively laborious; this is a framework capability that could unblock future Tapscript test-writing across the project independent of whether OP_CAT itself is ever activated.

uncertainties: Whether the #SCRIPT#/#CONTROLBLOCK# JSON test macros would be adopted or extracted independently of this PR's CAT-specific content; no evidence anyone has proposed splitting them out.

Whether 'consensus' for OP_CAT has shifted at all since the October 2024 Kill/Shill/Merge session; the discussion after that point is mostly clarifying edge cases, not revisiting the concept decision.
Exact current status of the linked bitcoin-inquisition activation, which is out of scope for this repo but cited as evidence of real-world testing.
result.card: This draft PR implements OP_CAT as a new Tapscript opcode (BIP-347), redefining OP_SUCCESS126, with two script-verify flags (SCRIPT_VERIFY_OP_CAT, SCRIPT_VERIFY_DISCOURAGE_OP_CAT) that a future soft fork could use for activation; it explicitly excludes any activation/signaling logic. It solves the problem that Bitcoin Core has no reference OP_CAT implementation for developers and researchers to build and test against, distinct from the bitcoin-inquisition signet fork where it has already run since April 2024. The strongest signal of its status: maintainer achow101 converted it to draft specifically because 'there does not appear to be consensus for the concept of OP_CAT in TapScript yet,' following a CoreDev Kill/Shill/Merge session, so the PR is paused on a project-level decision rather than on code quality. Reviewers who engaged on code details (rot13maxi, ajtowns, awin28522, Co1nB3e) had their points addressed, and a proposed 'neutered CAT' compromise from moonsettler was rebutted on technical grounds by bigspider. The author and co-contributor have recently signaled reduced attention (EthanHeilman: shifting to quantum-computing concerns until 2026), and there are no dependencies on other open PRs.
